title: Analysis of serum haptoglobin fucosylation in hepatocellular carcinoma and liver cirrhosis of different etiologies.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a specific glycan alteration (bifucosylated tetra‑antennary glycan on haptoglobin) that distinguishes HCC from cirrhosis, a clear disease biomarker claim. However, no quantitative performance metrics (AUC, sensitivity, etc.) are provided, so full text is needed to assess biomarker details.

title: Asymptomatic phosphomannose isomerase deficiency (MPI-CDG) initially mistaken for excessive alcohol consumption.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a glycan biomarker (carbohydrate‑deficient transferrin) whose abnormal pattern is linked to a specific disease (MPI‑CDG), providing quantitative enzyme activity and glycoform data that establish the association.

title: Abundance-ratio-based semiquantitative analysis of site-specific N-linked glycopeptides present in the plasma of hepatocellular carcinoma patients.

screening.reason: The abstract reports a specific glycan change (increased fucosylated vs non‑fucosylated VTN glycoforms) in HCC plasma versus normal plasma, indicating a potential diagnostic biomarker. However, quantitative details (sample size, statistical significance, effect size) are not provided, so full text is needed to assess the biomarker’s performance.

entities.evidence_sentence: Among these glycans, the abundance ratio of two representative glycoforms (fucosyl vs non-fucosyl) was significantly increased in HCC plasma relative to normal plasma.

title: Glycation of the complement regulatory protein CD59 is a novel biomarker for glucose handling in humans.

screening.reason: The study identifies soluble glycated CD59 (a glycan modification) as a biomarker associated with HbA1c, OGTT response, and insulin‑treatment–related glucose control, providing clear disease relevance and quantitative associations in humans.
